research_mode: official Building Safety Regulator and GOV.UK primary guidance only; safety-case, mandatory-occurrence, building-assessment-certificate and registration methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: BAC application duty
verified_claims: The PAP must apply for a building assessment certificate when BSR tells them to do so.
limitations: A PAP is not required to apply merely because a building has been registered.

sources.name: BAC building scope
verified_claims: The BAC regime covers registered high-rise residential buildings meeting the height or storey and residential-unit thresholds.
limitations: Thresholds do not establish that a particular structure is registered or in scope.

sources.name: BAC Part 4 assessment
verified_claims: BSR assesses whether the PAP is meeting legal duties under Part 4 of the Building Safety Act 2022.
limitations: Assessment of legal duties is not a parcel-level safety score.

sources.name: BAC application triggers
verified_claims: BSR may direct an application after registration or when an existing BAC needs reassessment.
limitations: The trigger date must come from a building-specific BSR direction.

sources.name: BAC contact-information duty
verified_claims: The PAP must keep BSR contact details current and notify BSR as soon as possible when a new PAP is expected.
limitations: Updated contact details do not prove transfer of legal responsibility is complete.

sources.name: BAC 28-day deadline
verified_claims: A directed BAC application must be submitted within 28 calendar days.
limitations: The deadline must be calculated from the actual direction date.

sources.name: BAC missed-deadline consequence
verified_claims: Missing the application deadline is a breach of duty and can lead to enforcement action.
limitations: Potential enforcement is not evidence that action has been taken.

sources.name: BAC and occupation separation
verified_claims: A registered high-rise residential building does not need a BAC before residents can live there.
limitations: This does not remove the separate requirement to register before occupation.

sources.name: BAC prioritisation criteria
verified_claims: BSR prioritises applications using building information such as height, residential-unit count and specified construction or cladding features.
limitations: Prioritisation does not constitute a final risk determination.

sources.name: BAC reassessment cycle
verified_claims: BSR aims to reassess a BAC about every five years and may reassess sooner after significant changes, incidents or safety-management issues.
limitations: An indicative cycle is not a guaranteed next-assessment date.

sources.name: BAC core document set
verified_claims: The application must include the resident engagement strategy, MOR-system information and safety case report.
limitations: Submitting documents does not prove their adequacy or implementation.

sources.name: BAC early preparation duty
verified_claims: The PAP must prepare the core documents as soon as the building is occupied or they become PAP, rather than waiting for a direction.
limitations: Early preparation cannot be inferred without document dates and evidence.

sources.name: BAC safety-case update notification
verified_claims: The PAP must tell BSR as soon as possible about safety-case updates covering new or increased risks or further risk controls.
limitations: Notification does not prove BSR has reviewed or accepted the update.

sources.name: BAC approval and display
verified_claims: BSR issues a BAC when satisfied with Part 4 compliance, and the certificate must be displayed prominently for residents.
limitations: A displayed certificate is not a permanent guarantee that risks are absent.

sources.name: BAC correction, refusal and review
verified_claims: BSR may allow prompt correction, refuse an application, require notices to be displayed, and permit review and tribunal appeal.
limitations: Availability of review or appeal does not imply the original decision was incorrect.
